extracted.intended_audience: merchants, bookkeepers, and students of commercial arithmetic (calculating interest/allocations)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and rules for computing 'merito' (interest) and allocating/bringing payments to common terms (year-end or other dates), including simple vs compound treatment, use of tables, and handling payments at multiple dates. The text is a practical manual for commercial/accounting computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: merito semplice (simple interest)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute interest simply for the time the money was employed (ordinary/simple interest), typically credited at the end of the year: interest is proportional to principal, rate, and time (fraction of year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text explains computing simple interest by taking the per-100 yearly rate and applying it to the principal for each year or fractional year; when merito is 'semplicimente' meritare a capo d'anno, sum the yearly interests for the specified years and months. Examples show summing per-year amounts and prorating for months (e.g., multiply by 6/12 for six months).

rubrics_metrics.name: merito composto (compound interest / capitalization of merito)
rubrics_metrics.description: When earned interest is added to the capital and itself earns further interest (capitalizing the merito), perform compounding — treat new capital (principal + merito) as basis for subsequent periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author demonstrates forming compounded amounts by adding earned merito to capital and then computing further interest on the enlarged sum, noting that repeated application yields 'doppie' (doubling effects) over multiple periods; suggests using multiplication (or tables) to compute repeated compounding rather than recomputing each year from the original principal.

rubrics_metrics.name: meritare a capo d'anno (crediting interest at yearly term)
rubrics_metrics.description: To credit interest 'a capo d'anno' (at year-ends), compute interest up to the chosen annual cut-off for each partida and either collect or carry interest to that yearly term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: for each payment/partita compute interest from its date to the year-end term (by prorating months/days), then sum those amounts; the text gives illustrative dated partite and shows how to bring individual meriti to the year term for aggregation and settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: meritare a capo di altro termine (crediting to arbitrary term/date)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the settlement term is not the year-end, bring amounts to the specified term by prorating or compounding for the interval between payment date and chosen term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author explains how to select any date (termino) and adjust each partida to that date by computing merito for the intervening time; includes examples of bringing payments to intermediate months/days and guidance on choosing the term for convenience and correctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: faldare la ragione / bring payments to a common term
rubrics_metrics.description: When payments occur at various dates, convert (faldare) each partida to a common date/term so they are comparable and aggregable — either by compounding forward or discounting back using the agreed rate and time fractions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive procedural guidance and dated examples: list each partita's date and amount, compute interest to the chosen common date, add (or subtract) accordingly, then aggregate capital + merito. The text emphasizes that this general method is reliable and avoids errors of ad hoc redistribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: use of merito & capitale tables (tauole del merito e capitale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare and use precomputed tables of merit and capital (per 100, per cent rates, and for multiple years) to speed and simplify calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author advises constructing tables (e.g., per 100 principal and rates up to e.g., 20%) showing yearly merito and compounded capitals through many years; shows how to read and multiply by table entries rather than recomputing each year. Tables are recommended for repeated/complex accounting tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: counting months/days and calendar variations
rubrics_metrics.description: Carefully count months and days according to the calendar conventions in force (different regional calendars and month-length conventions affect interest intervals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text notes differences of practice (Augustine, Egyptian, Roman conventions, etc.) and warns that the measure of movement (time) and the way months/years are partitioned matters for correct interest computation; adjust counting method to the local/customary calendar used in the transactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: handling partial periods and fractional-time proration
rubrics_metrics.description: For non-whole-year periods compute interest proportionally by months/days: multiply principal by rate and the fraction of the year that the money was employed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit examples show taking six months as 6/12, converting months within multi-year intervals, and multiplying/dividing by appropriate factors; also advises careful summation of monthly contributions when aggregating many small intervals.

rubrics_metrics.name: aggregation and allocation of capital and earned merit among parties
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple parties or partite are involved, sum capitals and meriti (after bringing each to the common term) and then allocate shares or settle balances according to the parties' respective capitals and accrued merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The procedure: (1) bring each person's capital and any earned merito to the chosen date, (2) sum capitals and meriti separately or combined as required, (3) apportion the total or compute net due to each party. The text gives examples where previously-accumulated merito is merged into capital before apportionment.

rubrics_metrics.name: prefer general, infallible method over ad hoc adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Use systematic conversion of each partida to a chosen term (faldare) rather than removing or rearranging parts arbitrarily, which can produce errors; the general method is reliable for many cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author repeatedly recommends the method of bringing all entries to a common term (using tables or stepwise multiplication) as simpler and less error-prone than piecemeal arithmetic manipulations; several worked examples are presented to illustrate reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: arithmetic practice: per-cent basis, multipliers, and successive multiplication
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform calculations on a per-100 (percent) basis: use multipliers and successive multiplication/division to compute multi-year effects and to transform sums between different units/timeframes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance includes using 100 as base, multiplying by yearly-percentage factors, successive multiplications to reach long terms (e.g., multiply for several years), and how to split and recombine sums (examples with numbers and multipliers are offered).

rubrics_metrics.name: present-value vs future-value approach (discounting vs compounding)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide whether to move amounts forward to a future payment date (compounding) or backward to a valuation date (discounting) depending on settlement needs; apply the corresponding factor for the elapsed time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text implicitly distinguishes the operations: when you 'reca' (bring) money to a future term, compound it by the merito for the intervening time; when adjusting payments back to an earlier date, discount by the merito. Examples of both forward and backward adjustments are interspersed in the worked examples.
